title: How do we write an expression for each situation?
description: Three situations are turned into expressions with brackets. A market gets mangoes for seven days, a year of savings is found from one month, and a snail climbs by day and slips by night.
teaching_notes: One idea: find the part that repeats, write it in a bracket, and multiply by how many times it repeats. Watch for students who give the snail one day for every centimetre of the post.

video_script.why: The child writes an expression for each situation by finding the part that repeats and then counting how many times it repeats.
video_script.substitution: Find what happens in one day or one month, write it in a bracket, and multiply by the number of days or months.
video_script.anchor: Three story cards: a mango market, a year of savings, and a snail climbing a post
video_script.payoff_line: The answers are one hundred and forty kilograms, ninety six thousand rupees and eight days.

final_answer.spoken: the answers are one hundred and forty kilograms, ninety six thousand rupees and eight days

names.{{NAME_5}}: the child who supplies 9 kg of mangoes each day
names.{{NAME_6}}: the child who supplies 11 kg of mangoes each day
names.{{NAME_4}}: the child who earns 20000 rupees each month

never_show: a snail that climbs above the top of the post and then slips
maths_rules: (c) a full day and night gives 3 − 2 = 1 cm, so 7 days give 7 cm
(c) the next day the snail climbs 3 cm to reach 10 cm before the night, so 8 days
video_script.design: Three story cards stay on the board. Each is opened in turn: the repeating part goes in a bracket, and it is multiplied by the number of times it repeats.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; three cards: {{NAME_5}} and {{NAME_6}} with mango crates at a market, {{NAME_4}} with a money jar, and a snail at the foot of a post with a treat on top

marks.h1: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.h2: the mango market card appears with two crates
marks.h3: the money jar card and the snail card appear
marks.h4: a question mark glows over the three cards

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about three everyday situations.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>{{NAME_5}} and {{NAME_6}} supply mangoes to a market that opens on all seven days of a week.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>{{NAME_4}} saves money every month, and a snail climbs a post to reach a treat.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>We write an expression for each situation, and then find its value.

beats.on_screen: the three cards stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a day card repeated in a row, a month card repeated in a row, and a day-and-night card repeated in a row

marks.g1: one day card is drawn and copies slide out in a row
marks.g2: one month card and one day-and-night card are drawn the same way
marks.g3: a bracket is drawn around the first card of each row

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Each story has a small part that repeats. It repeats day after day, or month after month.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>First we find the part that repeats, and then we count how many times it repeats.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>A bracket lets us write that repeating part as one number.

beats.on_screen: Given: (a) 9 kg and 11 kg of mangoes a day, 7 days; (b) ₹20000 earned, ₹5000 rent, ₹5000 food, ₹2000 other, every month; (c) climbs 3 cm by day, slips 2 cm at night, post 10 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, {{NAME_5}} supplies nine kilograms a day and {{NAME_6}} supplies eleven kilograms a day.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>{{NAME_4}} earns twenty thousand rupees every month.
She spends five thousand on rent, five thousand on food and two thousand on other costs.
<bookmark mark='gv3'/>The snail climbs three centimetres by day and slips two centimetres at night. The post is ten centimetres high.

beats.on_screen: To find: an expression and its value for each story

marks.fd1: the words an expression and its value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to write an expression for each story and find its value.

marks.s11: 9 + 11 is written in a bracket for one day
marks.s13: the bracket becomes 20 and 7 × 20 is written

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, the mangoes, where one day gives nine plus eleven kilograms together.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>For seven days, the supply is seven times open bracket nine plus eleven close bracket.
<bookmark mark='s13'/>The bracket is twenty. The supply is seven times twenty kilograms.

marks.s21: the three costs are put in a bracket and become 12000

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, the savings, starting with the costs of one month.
Open bracket five thousand plus five thousand plus two thousand close bracket is twelve thousand.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>One month saves twenty thousand minus twelve thousand, which is eight thousand.
<bookmark mark='s23'/>In twelve months, the saving is twelve times eight thousand.

beats.on_screen: (c) one day and night: 3 − 2 = 1 cm; after 7 days: 7 × (3 − 2) = 7 cm; next day: 7 + 3 = 10 cm, the top

marks.s31: 3 − 2 = 1 cm is written for one day and night
marks.s32: 7 × (3 − 2) = 7 cm is written and the snail sits at 7 cm
marks.s33: the next climb of 3 cm is drawn and reaches the top at 10 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, the snail, which gains three minus two centimetres in a full day and night.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>After seven full days, it has gained seven times open bracket three minus two close bracket. That is seven centimetres.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>On the next day, it climbs three centimetres more. It reaches ten before the night.

beats.on_screen: check: (a) 7 × 9 + 7 × 11 has the same terms; (b) 12 × 20000 − 12 × 12000 = 240000 − 144000; (c) after 6 days 6 cm, then 6 + 3 = 9 cm, below 10

marks.s42: the income and cost of one year are written
marks.s43: the snail at 6 cm climbs to 9 cm, short of the top
marks.s44: the year of costs is written below the year of income

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, check each story another way.
For the mangoes, seven times nine plus seven times eleven uses the same terms.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>For the savings, a year of income is twelve times twenty thousand.
<bookmark mark='s44'/>A year of costs is twelve times twelve thousand. The difference is twelve lots of eight thousand, as before.
<bookmark mark='s43'/>For the snail, after six days it is at six centimetres, and the next climb reaches only nine. Seven days are not enough.

marks.a3: the days of the snail are counted as 7 and 1 more, giving 8 days

narration: <bookmark mark='a1'/>The answers are one hundred and forty kilograms, ninety six thousand rupees and eight days.
<bookmark mark='a2'/>Seven times twenty is one hundred and forty, and twelve times eight thousand is ninety six thousand.
<bookmark mark='a3'/>The snail needs seven days and one more day, which is eight days.
